source.title: Ships and Storms
source.summary: How Islamic merchants managed risk on the Indian Ocean without insurance or interest-based lending.
source.author: Islamic Economics
source.body_text: A dhow loaded with pepper and silk leaves Aden for Gujarat. The voyage takes weeks. Pirates, storms, and shipwrecks are real possibilities. How do you finance a journey when insurance is forbidden and charging interest is a sin? Islamic merchants solved this through mudaraba: one partner provides the capital, the other provides the labor and expertise, and they share the profit or loss. It was venture capital a thousand years before Silicon Valley. This episode follows the Indian Ocean trade routes and shows how the prohibition on gharar didn't prevent commerce; it created more equitable ways to share risk.
